justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Trains delivery of interventions with tier-1 evidence; cardiac rehab (Cochrane), COPD pulmonary rehab (McCarthy 2015), and ICU early mobilization (Schweickert 2009 Lancet; Tipping 2017). Outcomes flow from those interventions; the residency builds the competency to deliver them well.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Spans acute care, ICU, and outpatient cardiac/pulmonary rehab; broad within the cardiopulmonary niche, but concentrated in hospital settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Supports the inpatient/acute and CR reimbursement environment, but the residency itself unlocks no new billing codes.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: A full 12-month accredited residency; low time-efficiency, though typically stipended, with high downstream signal.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Academic medical centers, ICUs, and VA systems value and sometimes prefer residency-trained cardiopulmonary PTs.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Residency-trained clinicians manage high-acuity cardiopulmonary patients whose function and symptoms reliably improve with skilled care.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Effectively zero; cardiopulmonary PT is hospital/ICU/program-based and salaried.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: None; services bill under institutional/Medicare structures with no individual premium.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Strong differentiation within the narrow specialty job market; near-invisible outside it.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Very low; an employed-clinician, institutional pathway, not a private-practice ownership play.
justifications.business.marketDemand: No direct-to-consumer demand; demand is institutional.
justifications.business.efficiency: A 12-month residency is the least business-efficient path here, justified by clinical/academic signal rather than ROI.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: ABPTRFE accreditation is a top academic/clinical signal in PT; residency completion is highly regarded for faculty and specialty roles.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Residencies require scholarship/EBP projects and immersion in the strong cardiopulmonary literature base.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: A direct on-ramp to clinical-instructor, residency-mentor, and DPT faculty roles.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Built on deep domain evidence (Cochrane cardiac/pulmonary rehab, ICU-mobility RCTs); credential-specific outcome evidence remains limited.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Cardiopulmonary faculty are chronically scarce; residency-trained PTs are highly sought.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Low acquisition efficiency (a full residency year), but high academic payoff in recognition and faculty demand.
